copies.headline: Adam Drafted Like A Defending Champion
copies.body: Nobody's played a snap, so this is a pure roster take, and Adam's cabin weekend was ruthless: an 89 draft grade, T-2nd of 12, and a lineup projecting 120 a week, 3rd of 12. Jaxon Smith-Njigba at 19 is the anchor, Jayden Daniels and Brock Purdy give him a QB room nobody else needs to worry about, and Kenneth Walker III, Rico Dowdle and Bucky Irving mean the RB spot is a preference, not a problem. Sam LaPorta is questionable, and Mark Andrews is right there. Week 1 he opens at 116 against Logan. The defending champ and the best career record in league history, still not making mistakes.

copies.headline: Christian Drafted Depth, Now Bring The Aura
copies.body: Christian walked out of the cabin with an 89 draft grade, tied for 2nd in the league, and it's easy to see why: CeeDee Lamb and DeVonta Smith is a real receiver room, Chase Brown and Travis Etienne Jr. is a functional backfield, and the roster index of 55 says the board respects it. The nitpick is the top: Trevor Lawrence at 17 projected points is fine, not scary, and George Kittle is already questionable in August. The 118 weekly projection ranks 5th of 12, so #2 is a bet on the roster, not a coronation. Week 1 draws Peter.

copies.headline: Best Draft On Paper, Eighth-Best Projection
copies.body: Peter walked out of the cabin with the best draft in the league — 89 out of 100, 1st of 12 — and somehow the math still shrugs. Lamar Jackson and Bijan Robinson are a top-two you build a season around, but the 117-a-week projection ranks 8th of 12, largely because Jonathon Brooks, Tee Higgins and Tucker Kraft are all carrying questionable tags before a snap. Roster index 55, third on the board. The career PF leader with 7,046.6 doesn't need convincing that talent scores. He needs it healthy.

copies.headline: Logan Drafted A Contender, Which Is The Problem
copies.body: Fourth on the board, 120 a week projected out of the best lineup, and a draft that graded 86 — sixth of twelve — because Logan stacked the Eagles backfield and let the roster index (52) do the arguing. Hurts at 21, Barkley at 18, Jefferson at 17. That's a real spine. The trouble is history: two straight top seeds in 2023 and 2024, zero playoff wins, then a 4-10 dress fitting last year. He opens at 123 against Adam, who broke the curse Logan couldn't. Cruel scheduling.

copies.headline: Kaleb's 86 Draft Comes With Injury Tape
copies.body: Kaleb drafted well — 86 out of 100, tied for 4th of 12 — and yet the projection reads 118 a week, 6th of 12, which is what happens when four of your best pieces have a QUESTIONABLE tag stapled to them. Ashton Jeanty and Breece Hall are 18 and 16 points of upside and a weekly coin flip. Justin Herbert to Ladd McConkey is a real spine, Drake London is a real WR1, Harold Fannin Jr. at 11 is fine. The 2023 worst-to-first champ knows how to survive a mess. Week 1 he's at 119 against Isaac.

copies.headline: Noah Drafted Well, Projects Terribly, Wins Anyway
copies.body: Noah's draft graded out at 86, tied for 4th, and then the projection model looked at the same names and put this roster 12th of 12 at 116 a week. Achane and Cook give him 33 points of backfield before anyone else shows up, which is nice, because after Garrett Wilson the receiving room is a questionable Mike Evans and a Michael Wilson at 10. Colston Loveland at 12 is a real tight end bet. Week 1 projects 113 against John. Noah has never cared about regular seasons anyway — five playoff wins say so.

copies.headline: Best Lineup In The League, Worst Draft Grade
copies.body: Leif somehow drafted the highest-projecting starting lineup in the league — 123 a week, 1st of 12 — and still walked out of the cabin with an 80 draft grade, dead last of 12. That's the Joey Lunchbox special: Josh Allen, Christian McCaffrey, Derrick Henry and Davante Adams up top, then a cliff you can hear from the lake. The roster index sits at 47, barely below average, because depth exists. McCaffrey and Mahomes are both questionable already. Week 1 projects 118 against Mitchell. Top-heavy works until it doesn't.

copies.headline: Nico Found, Everything Else Still Missing
copies.body: The team name says Mitchell knows what he wants, and to be fair, he got him — Nico Collins at 16 projected is a real anchor, and Jahmyr Gibbs at 22 is the kind of pick you build a season around. The problem is everything after that. This roster projects 116 a week, 11th of 12, which is what happens when your QB room is Jaxson Dart and Daniel Jones and two of your best pass-catchers, Tyler Warren and Rachaad White, are already tagged questionable. The 85 draft grade, 7th of 12, was generous. Week 1 against Leif projects 117. Bring a coat.

copies.headline: Amon-Ra Carries, Everyone Else Coughs
copies.body: Grant's team name is the best joke in the league and Amon-Ra St. Brown is the only player on it doing something genuinely funny at 19 projected. The rest is a wheeze: 120 a week from the best lineup, which is 2nd of 12, so the ceiling is real even if the path there is Kyler Murray and Baker Mayfield both projecting 16 and neither inspiring a single confident breath. Omarion Hampton at 18 is nice. Draft grade of 80, T-9th of 12, says the middle of this roster is thin. Week 1 against CJ tells us fast.

copies.headline: CJ Bet The Cabin On Burrow
copies.body: The team name promised a Burrow-centric operation and CJ delivered, right down to the 18-point projection that everyone else's QB1 also happens to hit. The problem is what's behind him: a 116-a-week lineup projection, 9th of 12, built on Jonathan Taylor doing the heavy lifting and then a whole lot of Parker Washington at 11. Emeka Egbuka's already tagged questionable, which is a strange way to enter a season nobody has played yet. Draft night graded out 83, 8th of 12 — the roster index of 48 is the honest read. Week 1 says 118 against Grant.

copies.headline: John Drafted The Rams And Stopped There
copies.body: John's draft night looked like a Ram-fan bender: Matthew Stafford, Kyren Williams, Puka Nacua, Blake Corum, plus D'Andre Swift and Caleb Williams to keep the Chicago half of the theme alive. It graded out at 80, T-9th of 12, and the roster index sits at 45 — below average, which is exactly what a 117-a-week projection (7th of 12) reads like. The tight ends are genuinely good; Brock Bowers and Trey McBride both start on most rosters. The problem is everything past Nacua, who's already questionable. Week 1 projects 122 against Noah, the postseason assassin. Beating Peter is still the only trophy John reliably wins.

copies.headline: Isaac Drafted Two Question Marks and Hoped
copies.body: Isaac's roster projects 116 a week, 10th of 12, which is what happens when your ceiling is Ja'Marr Chase at 20 and your floor is asking whether Chase and Malik Nabers, both tagged questionable, feel like showing up. Behind them it's Bo Nix at 16 and a running back committee — Javonte Williams, Cam Skattebo, Jaylen Warren — that tops out at 15. T.J. Hockenson and Dalton Kincaid both project nine, so the tiebreaker is vibes. The draft graded 80, T-9th. Week 1 says 117 against Kaleb. Bring a nice dress.

intro: Adam takes the top spot at 55.8, though the gap between him and Christian at 55.0 is thinner than the number of syllables in their names — and Peter's 89.1 draft grade is actually the best in the league, so the podium is functionally a coin flip. Isaac sits at the bottom on a 44.6 score and an 80.5 draft, the same draft grade as Grant and John, which is a rough club to be the worst member of. The interesting shuffle is Leif, who jumped two spots to seventh despite the weakest draft on the board at 79.5, entirely because his roster projects for 123 a week — the highest mark in the league by four points. Whether that projection survives contact with actual football is the question, but on paper he's the only team here with a top-end weekly ceiling and a bottom-end resume to match.
nudges: Leif +2: Roster projects 1st in league at 123/week; ranked 9th.
Grant +1: Projects 2nd in league at 120/week; ranked 10th.
